purpose: Board energy of single-GPU Llama-3.1-8B serving and ResNet-50 training on four more boards of each device, measured against MLSys·im's two device-power assumptions (rated TDP and Engine.solve's energy-proportional rule) with the protocol of ../gpu-energy/. It asks how much energy differs between boards of one device, and whether the change between ../gpu-energy/ and ../gpu-energy-workloads/ comes from the boards or from the seed.
declaration_note: The devices, workloads, engine settings, configurations and efficiencies are those of ../gpu-energy-workloads/ for Llama-3.1-8B and ResNet-50 training. Only the seed differs: 2193, the seed of ../gpu-energy/. None is fitted to measurements. Commit this file before any run: each run manifest records its SHA-256, and the analysis refuses runs measured under a different plan.
analysis_note: Declared before any run. analyze_gpu_energy.py reports the four estimates and device_choice.csv for these runs, as for the other two tests. compare_gpu_energy_boards.py writes each verified run's energy per unit of work from all three tests to board_energy.csv, and the comparisons below to board_summary.csv. The questions are: (1) for each configuration, how much energy per unit of work differs between boards of one device measured with seed 2193 (this test's boards, and the H100 and A100 boards of ../gpu-energy/); (2) whether the boards of ../gpu-energy-workloads/, measured with seed 2198, fall inside that range; (3) for each Llama-3.1-8B decode configuration, on how many pairings of one H100 board and one A100 board the H100 uses less energy, over this test's boards and over every board of the three tests; (4) whether this test's runs repeat the answers of ../gpu-energy-workloads/ on decode power, offsetting errors and device choice. The answers are reported whichever way they go.
runs_note: Four runs per device, each in its own container, launched together. A run that the runner refuses because the device does not match expected_name is excluded and launched again, until each device has four measured runs. Every run is used, whichever board it lands on.
boundary: GPU board only, as reported by NVML. Excludes host CPU, DRAM, NICs, fans outside the board, power-supply losses, and facility overhead (PUE).
split_note: Every configuration is held out: nothing is fitted to these runs.

llama31_8b.weights_note: An ungated mirror of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, used under the Llama 3.1 Community License. At these revisions its config, generation config, tokenizer, and weight index are byte-identical to meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B@d04e592bb4f6aa9cfee91e2e20afa771667e1d4b (equal git blob ids), and its four weight shards match that revision's sizes and the SHA-256 of unsloth/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B. Meta does not publish the shard hashes without a license acceptance. The download is checked against weights_sha256 before any GPU starts.
llama31_8b.engine: vLLM offline engine (LLM.generate), one GPU, CUDA graphs for decode, greedy, ignore_eos, random prompt tokens, all requests of a batch submitted together
llama31_8b.model_seq_len_note: ServingModel is evaluated at seq_len = prompt_tokens + output_tokens // 2, the mean context length over the decode phase, for ITL; prefill uses seq_len = prompt_tokens.

resnet50_train.engine: torchvision resnet50, SGD, torch.autocast fp16, channels_last, synthetic on-device data

configs.efficiency_note: No H200 anchor exists. The H100 value is used: the registry gives both the same 989 TFLOP/s dense FP16 peak.
